services.name: Boat Tour
services.desc: Not everyone crosses the causeway wanting adrenaline. This is a thirty-minute guided run out of Dinner Key at a pace that lets you look around, take photographs that aren't blurred, and hear what you're looking at. The captain covers the marina, the shoreline and whatever the bay decides to show you - manatees and dolphins are common enough that regulars stop being surprised. No age minimum, no swimming, no equipment. It's the one grandparents, toddlers and everyone in between can do on the same boat, and it works well as the opening act for a group where half the party is booked on something faster afterwards. services.name: Parasailing
services.desc: The bay view nobody gets from the sand - a short ride off the Beach and you're airborne over Biscayne Bay. You can see the water from your balcony on Miami Beach. This is how you get above it. The trip runs about an hour on the boat, of which five to ten minutes are spent hanging under the canopy at up to four hundred feet, with Key Biscayne on one side and the downtown skyline on the other. You leave from Pier 9 at Dinner Key Marina - a fifteen-minute drive from South Beach - because the bay there sits behind the barrier islands and stays flyable on afternoons when the ocean side is too churned up to launch.
